articles.title: MAI Code 2 vs Claude Opus 5.5 vs GPT-6.1 Sol: "5% of the Cost" Is a Promo Price
articles.summary:
Microsoft says MAI Code 2 gives you 96% of Claude Opus 5.5's coding performance at 5% of the cost, and 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol at 40%. articles.title: AI agent REST API errors: what HiveGate 0.4.0 changes
articles.summary:
An agent API can fail in a way that is worse than going down: it answers. The provider rejects the key, the account is out of credits, or the model is unavailable, and the API still returns 200 OK with the provider's error text where the answer should be. A chat UI shows it to the user as if the agent said it. An eval scores it. A retry loop sees success and stops retrying. A cost report counts it as a completed conversation.

articles.title: Claude Code forgets your sessions after 30 days. I found my year anyway.
articles.summary:
I wanted to see my year with Claude Code the way Spotify shows me a year of music. So I built agent-wrapped:



npx github:openyard-cloud/agent-wrapped






It reads the history Claude Code (and Codex) already keep on your computer and writes one HTML file: a short story you tap through, and a card you can save as an image. Here is mine.



Nothing is uploaded. The page makes no network requests, and the card shows totals only.

The first version said I had 71 active days this year. The real number is 126. Finding the other 55 is most of this post.

articles.title: OpenAPI JSON Schema Differences
articles.summary:
Quick answer: OpenAPI does not run on the full JSON Schema standard. It borrows JSON Schema's structure and changes a few keywords, so some valid JSON Schema constructs fail in OpenAPI and vice versa. OpenAPI 3.0 uses an extended subset of an early draft with its own rules, while 3.1 aligns with JSON Schema 2020-12; the differences that bite teams are null handling, numeric bounds, $ref siblings, and the type field.

articles.title: Choosing a PaaS Provider Canadian Businesses Can Rely On
articles.summary:
Platform as a service (PaaS) lets your team build, deploy, and run applications without managing servers, operating systems, or much of the underlying infrastructure. For Canadian businesses, that convenience comes with extra questions. Where will our data live? Which privacy laws apply? What happens if the provider has an outage, changes its pricing, or is subject to foreign legal demands?

This guide explains what to look for in a PaaS provider, the Canadian-specific issues to check, how to compare costs, and how to run a selection process that holds up.

articles.title: Ten Years On, Google Updates the SRE Book for the AI Era
articles.summary: Google has announced a completely rewritten second edition of Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems, ten years after the original book was published by O'Reilly Media.
